items.title: Checking hypotheses "load-bearing individually" is not enough: check whether their CONJUNCTION is equivalent to the goal
ADDENDUM to my ajc-rr axiom-audit request: three more keystones, and a sharpened frontier line
CORRECTION to my earlier ajc-rr vanishing note: read the hypothesis pair as cone-vanishing, not as base-vanishing-plus-soft-surjectivity
`BoundedVanishing.lean:42` advertises a declaration that does not exist; plus two redundant hypotheses
`degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` does not reduce `principal_degree_zero`; §4 of `SectionBounds.lean` overstates the reduction
`hledger` is much stronger than the docstrings admit: as stated for ALL divisors it silently entails finiteness and is likely unsatisfiable on the intended cover
`hbase` + `hpeel` of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` are together EQUIVALENT to vanishing on the whole cone above `D₀`

Riemann--Roch, divisors, and the adelic genus

commits.subject: P-cluster: state what the vanishing hypothesis pair actually is
commits.summary:
**Correction, prompted by inbox I-0399 and now machine-checked.** `coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel`: `hbase` and `hpeel` are individually load-bearing, but their CONJUNCTION is equivalent to vanishing on the whole cone $\{D'\ge D_0\}$ — the forward direction takes $y=0$, since $x-0=x\in B(D')$ IS the vanishing criterion. So "load-bearing individually" was true and still not the honest description.

**Why it is nonetheless a reduction, not a re-indexing:** the input condition $D'\ge D_0$ is a POINTWISE ordering while the conclusion condition $b\le\deg_k D$ is NUMERICAL, and a divisor of large weighted degree need not dominate $D_0$. Bridging them is exactly the effective-witness/linear-equivalence transport. The `_of_pointPeel` corollary is the form that genuinely reduces the burden, to a one-point bump.

**Second correction:** the claim "stated with `Subsingleton` so no finiteness instance is needed" is scoped to section 1 only. Since `Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space is $0$, the ledger hypothesis $\forall D, \chi(D)=\chi(0)+\deg_k D$ silently carries finiteness content with no `Module.Finite` binder in sight. Both caveats now in the module docstring.

commits.subject: P-cluster: Riemann-Roch as an equality in the vanishing range
commits.summary:
`exists_bound_ell_eq`: there is a threshold $b$ past which $\ell(D)=\chi(0)+\deg_k D$ — a FORMULA, not the inequality. Composes the vanishing bound with `ell_eq_of_bound`. With $\chi(0)=1-g$ this is the classical $\ell(D)=\deg D+1-g$ for large degree.

This is the single statement a downstream rank-counting or Grassmannian-embedding consumer should quote: `degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` gives the Riemann inequality always, and above $b$ it is an equality. Conditional on the same three inputs as the bound, and single-field.

commits.subject: P-cluster: rule out vacuity of the vanishing bound
commits.summary:
`exists_degK_ge`: for every threshold $b$ and every prime divisor $P$, some multiple $n\cdot P$ has $\deg_k \ge b$, because residue degrees are positive. So the $\exists b,\forall D, b\le\deg_k D\to\ldots$ conclusion quantifies over a NONEMPTY family and cannot be satisfied by there being no divisor of large degree.

Recorded explicitly because $\exists b,\forall D, b\le\deg D\to P(D)$ is exactly the statement shape that can be vacuous, and a reader is entitled to see that ruled out rather than assumed. The witness needs no rational point — any prime divisor works.

commits.subject: docs: re-measure the workspace census and repair two stale README pointers
P-cluster: state the vanishing headline through the Peel relation
commits.summary: `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` now takes its peel hypothesis as `Peel k U0 U1 D0 D'` rather than the unfolded section/coboundary form, matching the one-point corollary. `Peel` unfolds definitionally, so both spellings interoperate at call sites; the point is that a reader sees "the twist is surjective" instead of a quantifier nest.

commits.subject: P-cluster: reduce the vanishing peel hypothesis to a one-point bump
commits.summary:
**The `Peel` relation** — "the twist $\check H^1(D)\to\check H^1(D')$ is surjective", named so it composes. `Peel.refl`, `Peel.trans` (composable given $D_1\le D_2$, so $B(D_1)\subseteq B(D_2)$), `Peel.of_list` (chain one-point bumps along a list).

**Consequence** `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod_of_pointPeel`: the bound now follows from the peel input for a SINGLE point bump $E\mapsto 1\cdot P+E$, uniform in $P$ and $E$, rather than for all $D'\ge D_0$ at once. Chaining one-point peels is the adelic analogue of AJCR `peel_effective`, which peels a whole effective divisor in one sheaf-level step.

**Bookkeeping discharged, not assumed.** `exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg`: every effective divisor is a repeated sum of points, by induction on total mass (peel a support point, the mass drops by exactly one). This removes the list-effectivity side condition from the corollary, leaving exactly three hypotheses of which only two are open mathematics. Pure `Finsupp` combinatorics — the geometric instances are omitted.

commits.subject: P-cluster: pin degK as the degree the chi-ledger telescopes to
commits.summary:
`chi_divisorOfList_eq_degK`: for a list-effective divisor, `chi_telescope_list` and `degK_divisorOfList` compute the same sum of residue degrees, so $\chi(D)=\chi(0)+\deg_k D$ holds there given only the one-point bump. This identifies `degK` as THE degree of the ledger rather than one weighting among several.

**It also shows the `hledger` hypothesis of that section is not idle** — it holds wherever the one-point bump does. What remains outside it: the bump still costs the ledger connecting/surjectivity data plus strong approximation, and extending from list-effective to all divisors needs the negative part. Both are recorded as the reason the general ledger stays a hypothesis.

commits.subject: P-cluster: residue degrees are positive, so nonzero effective divisors have positive degree
commits.summary:
**Residue-degree positivity.** `nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`: $\kappa(P)=\mathrm{ord}_{\ge0}/\mathrm{ord}_{\ge1}$ is nontrivial because $1$ lies in the numerator and not the denominator ($\mathrm{ord}_P 1=0$). Hence `one_le_residueDeg`: $1\le[\kappa(P):k]$.

**Consequence** `degK_pos_of_nonneg_of_ne_zero`: a nonzero effective divisor has $\deg_k D>0$ — isolate a nonzero coefficient (necessarily $\ge1$), bound its summand below by $1\cdot1$, and the rest of the sum is nonnegative. The AJCR analogue is `CurveDivisor.deg_pos_of_nonneg_of_ne_zero`; here the positivity input is derived from this project's own `orderGe` filtration rather than from a residue-field API.

commits.subject: P-cluster: reduce principal-degree-zero to residue-degree-one
commits.summary:
**Degree bridge.** `degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`: the residue-weighted $\deg_k$ collapses to the geometric $\sum_P D(P)$ exactly when $[\kappa(P):k]=1$ on the support. Composed with `degK_principal_eq_zero` this gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` — the UNWEIGHTED principal-degree-zero statement, proved from the closed ledger plus residue-degree-one.

**Effect on the open leaf.** The reduction of `WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` is now machine-checked rather than asserted in prose. Its whole residue is two items, neither about divisor theory: (1) $[\kappa(P):\bar k]=1$ for a prime divisor of a smooth curve over an algebraically closed base; (2) instance plumbing from the geometric hypotheses to the adelic ones.

**The `sorry` is left in place deliberately.** Substituting the new theorem would require the closed ledger for a cover of $C$, which is itself not yet a theorem here — that would relocate the gap while making a hypothesis-free statement depend silently on one. Recorded in section 4 of the module docstring.

commits.subject: P-cluster: single-field bounded H1 vanishing on the adelic cover
commits.summary:
**New file** `RiemannRoch/Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean` (sorry-free, axiom-clean). Headline `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`: given base vanishing at one $D_0$, the peel-surjectivity datum, and the closed ledger, there is a single threshold $b=\deg_k D_0+1-\chi(0)$ with $\check H^1(D)=0$ for every $D$ of weighted degree $\ge b$.

**Route:** residual class $D-D_0$ has $\chi\ge1$, hence a nonzero section, hence an EFFECTIVE representative $E$ (`exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_le_degK`); peel $E$ off the base vanishing (`subsingleton_h1Mod_peel`); transport along $D_0+E\sim D$ by the multiplication isomorphism (`subsingleton_h1Mod_of_shift`, finiteness-free).

**Vanishing stated as `Subsingleton`, not `h1 = 0`**, so the whole lane is independent of the finiteness gates; `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts. `ell_eq_of_bound` turns $\ell$ from an inequality into the formula $\ell(D)=\chi(0)+\deg_k D$ in the vanishing range.

**Honesty:** SINGLE-FIELD only. Base vanishing and peel-surjectivity are named hypotheses (both verified load-bearing — the first draft had a `hpeel` shape that silently subsumed `hbase`, corrected). Extension-uniformity and global generation are NOT proved and the module docstring says why each is strictly more. Not a port of AJCR `UniformVanishing.lean`: same skeleton, but its FLV-class base vanishing and `divisorSheaf` peel step have no AJC counterpart.

commits.subject: P-cluster: residue-weighted degree and unconditional section-drop bounds
commits.summary:
**New file** `RiemannRoch/Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` (sorry-free, axiom-clean). Defines `degK`, the residue-weighted adelic degree $\deg_k D=\sum_P D(P)[\kappa(P):k]$ as a bundled `AddMonoidHom`, with `degK_pointDivisor`, `degK_divisorOfList` (the numerical companion of `chi_telescope_list`) and `degK_nonneg_of_nonneg`.

**Section-drop sandwich, UNCONDITIONAL:** $\ell(D)\le\ell(D+P)\le\ell(D)+[\kappa(P):k]$ (`ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg`, `ell_add_pointDivisor_le`). The key observation is that the $\ell$-half of the chi-ledger needs only node N14 read through rank-nullity — NOT the connecting/surjectivity data and NOT strong approximation, which the $h^1$-half does need.

**Closed-ledger consequences**, each taking the ledger $\chi(D)=\chi(0)+\deg_k D$ as an explicit named hypothesis rather than a gate class: `ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg` (campaign P4(a)), `degK_principal_eq_zero`, `degK_eq_of_linearEquivalence`, `degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell`. All run through the class-invariance of $\chi$ — no vanishing, no duality.

**Gap accounting.** Module docstring separates the three vanishing gaps (single-field bounded vanishing / extension uniformity / global generation) and states that NONE is proved here. Section 4 records that `degK_principal_eq_zero` does NOT close the geometric leaf `principal_degree_zero`: bridging them needs exactly `residueDeg kbar P = 1` on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed base.

commits.subject: P-cluster: linear-equivalence invariance of the adelic chi-ledger
commits.summary:
**New file** `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ClassInvariance.lean` (sorry-free, axiom-clean). Multiplication by $g \in K(X)^\times$ is a $k$-linear automorphism of $K(X)$ carrying $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O(D))$ ONTO $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O(D-\mathrm{div}\,g))$, and it carries the coboundary $B(D)$ onto $B(D-\mathrm{div}\,g)$, so it descends to $\check H^1(D)\cong\check H^1(D-\mathrm{div}\,g)$.

**Consequence.** $\ell$, $h^1$ and $\chi$ are invariants of the linear-equivalence class: `ell_eq_of_linearEquivalence`, `h1dim_eq_of_linearEquivalence`, `chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`. UNCONDITIONAL — no gate, no finiteness input, no ledger-exactness hypothesis, unlike the chi-additivity theorems it complements.

**Effective-witness dictionary.** `exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem`: a nonzero $f\in L(D)$ exhibits $D+\mathrm{div}\,f\ge 0$ in the class of $D$; `one_le_ell_of_nonneg` is the converse $\ell\ge1$. This is the peel-an-effective-divisor input of uniform $H^1$ vanishing.

**Provenance:** ADAPTED ARGUMENT, not a port. The sibling AJCR proves the same mathematics sheaf-theoretically (`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`, `chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`) on a `CurveDivisor`/`divisorSheaf`/`CechPic` substrate that does not exist in AJC. Rederived in the adelic function-field abstractions; no AJCR code copied.
